clue.text: Person who digs a gambling game?

definitions.meaning: someone who digs another in the ribs prods or pokes them, so is one who pokes
a card game played for stakes, with betting and bluffing

explanation.surface: A riddle asking who the digger is that also names a card game played for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one who prods with a finger, and the card game of bluff and betting.

clue.text: Odd points identifying part of engine

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of points are rearranged

explanation.surface: Odd features help identify a component of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The cylinder plunger that moves up and down in an engine is an example of a part.

clue.text: Do as promised — retain a single weapon

parts.note: to keep something is to retain it
a single thing is one
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: A knight told to retain his only weapon does as he promised.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for honouring a pledge, doing exactly what you said you would.

clue.text: One providing information on malt liquor?

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
porter is a dark beer brewed from malt

explanation.surface: Someone tells you all about a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who gathers and passes on news to the public.

clue.text: Small untruth about teetotal Liberal

indicators.note: about means around, so the falsehood surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a lie is an untruth
TT stands for teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: A fib told about a politician who does not drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms describing something of modest size.

clue.text: Put money on a Greek character

parts.note: to bet is to stake money on an outcome

explanation.surface: Someone gambles on a person from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet; character here means letter.

clue.text: Like a star in last rally

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sporting star shines in a closing rally.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the stars, so starlike or stellar.

clue.text: In mire, spied damaged layer of skin

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a bog notices their skin has been hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: The outermost layer of the skin, over the dermis, is its medical name.

clue.text: Be quick — teasing the dog may do this!

definitions.text: teasing the dog may do this!
definitions.meaning: a teased dog may well start to snap, so this makes it snappy

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an order to hurry; literally, provoking a dog causes it to snap.

clue.text: Slumber an old PM's rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister; with the possessive S this gives PEELS

explanation.surface: A former prime minister turns down the chance of a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns PEELS backwards. Robert Peel was British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms: both mean the restful state of being asleep.

clue.text: Unfashionable sponsor, one dwelling in the bush

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
a backer supports or funds a venture

explanation.surface: A sponsor who is behind the times turns out to live in the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: The bush is the Australian outback, the remote interior of that country.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in the remote Australian interior, known as the bush, is so called.

clue.text: News about union leader's sister

indicators.note: about means around, so the two letters surround the next piece

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, so news, as plural, is two Ns

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of union is taken

explanation.surface: A news report about a trade union boss's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the U from 'union leader's' between the two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a religious order is addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Dreary routine to, at first, study John Stuart?

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word to

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was the Victorian philosopher, so his surname is wanted

explanation.surface: Studying the philosopher John Stuart Mill is presented as a tedious chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a monotonous round of work that goes nowhere, like walking on an exercise machine.

clue.text: Ailment riders do suffer

indicators.note: to suffer is to be harmed or knocked about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Riders do suffer from a particular illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder is a medical illness or complaint; synonyms.

clue.text: Removes non-representational paintings

definitions.meaning: to abstract something is to take it away or extract it
works of art that do not depict recognisable objects

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is take away; the noun sense is artworks that do not show real things.

clue.text: Attraction priests originally found in a set of bells

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the bells

parts.note: a peal is a set of bells tuned to ring together

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word priests

explanation.surface: Priests find something attractive about a church's bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm or allure, the quality that draws people in; synonym.

clue.text: Spike of flowers in mosaic at Kingsville

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mosaic in a town called Kingsville shows a spray of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangling spike of tiny flowers on trees such as willow and hazel.

clue.text: Farm animal that makes us scatter?

definitions.meaning: an imperative telling us to scatter seed over the ground

explanation.surface: A farmyard creature that sends people running.
explanation.definitionFit: A female pig is one sense; the verb meaning to scatter seed is the other.

clue.text: Summons he delivered, making us squirm

parts.note: a writ is a legal document such as a summons

explanation.surface: A man delivers a court summons, which makes people squirm.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist and wriggle in discomfort; synonyms.

clue.text: One who demonstrates in favour of examiner

parts.note: pro means for, or in favour of
a tester examines or checks things

explanation.surface: A demonstration is held in support of an exam official.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes part in a public demonstration against something.

clue.text: Make an impression, and so on, with husband

parts.note: etc is short for et cetera, meaning and so on

explanation.surface: Someone and her husband try to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave a design into a surface, literally making an impression in it.

clue.text: Girl keeping record in warehouse

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the name holds the record inside it

parts.note: Dot is a girl's name, short for Dorothy
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A young woman stores a record in a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A storage building for goods or supplies; synonyms.

clue.text: Habit-forming preservative, say, going round clubs

indicators.note: going round means enclosing, so the substance surrounds the card suit letter

parts.note: a preservative is an example of a food additive, hence say
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A chemical preservative used in clubs is said to cause dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug or pastime that causes dependence is described this way; synonym.

clue.text: Verse initially reconciling him, you and me

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the following three words

explanation.surface: A poem begins by bringing the speaker, him and you together.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry with matching end-sounds, or a short poem, can be called verse.
